speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or a rash elsewhere on your body? Also, when did these symptoms first appear, and have you had any recent sun exposure or new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The combination of blisters on your forearm, oral ulcers causing pain when eating, and vaginal ulcers causing pain during intercourse is very specific. Given your recent change in medications, have you noticed any other skin lesions like target-like spots, or any eye pain/redness? Also, is the pain in your mouth severe enough to stop you from eating solid foods?

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) induced by Captopril.

The history of recent captopril initiation combined with skin blisters, oral ulcers, and genital ulcers is highly specific for SJS. Cellulitis does not present with mucosal involvement or widespread blistering. I recommend stopping the captopril immediately and initiating supportive care. If you have a fever, I will request a CBC and blood cultures to rule out secondary infection.
